mainTopic: Whether the משנה about a forgotten מנחה vow can follow רבי שמעון, who allows bringing a קרבן with a condition, and how his half-and-half offering works
overview: This amud finishes quoting רבי שמעון's case of a person who is not sure he is a מצורע. He brings one animal with a condition: if he is a מצורע it is his אשם, and if not it is a שלמי נדבה. The animal follows the strict rules of both offerings, so its meat is eaten for only one day and a night. The גמרא uses this case to show that the משנה about a forgotten מנחה vow can follow רבי שמעון, who allows a condition on a קרבן. It brings up an answer from מסכת זבחים: רבי שמעון allows such a condition from the start only to help a person become טהור. The גמרא replies that this limit applies only to שלמים, where the condition shortens the eating time, while with מנחות a condition is fine even from the start. רב פפא then asks how רבי שמעון's half-and-half offering can work, since each offering would come from two separate עשרונות and לוגין, and אביי answers that רבי שמעון holds this is valid. The גמרא explains how the person sets conditions on his handfuls (קמיצה), and then begins a new challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The condition the doubtful מצורע makes
steps.stepSummary: The person brings an animal and a לוג of oil and says: if I am a מצורע, this is my אשם and this is my לוג; if not, this animal is a שלמי נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings the animal and the oil with it and says: 'If I am a מצורע, this is my אשם and this is my לוג. If not, let this אשם be a voluntary שלמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of רבי שמעון's rule about someone who does not know if he is a מצורע. He brings one animal with a two-way condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One animal is set aside to fit either situation. If he is a מצורע, it counts as his אשם; if he is not, it becomes a שלמים. This is how he can finish his purification even though his status is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who must bring special offerings to become טהור
A guilt offering; a מצורע brings one as part of his purification
A measure of oil that the מצורע brings with his אשם
A voluntary peace offering

phrases.english: with it, and says:
phrases.notes: This starts mid-sentence: 'it' is his אשם, which he brings along with its לוג of oil before making this condition.

phrases.english: If he is a leper —
phrases.notes: He is talking about himself: 'if I am a מצורע.'

phrases.english: this is his guilt offering and this is his log,
and if not —
this guilt offering shall be a gift peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote of רבי שמעון's ruling that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון allows bringing a קרבן with a condition when one is unsure what he owes, so the case of the מנחות can follow him
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's rule about the doubtful מצורע

steps.title: The doubtful animal follows the strict rules of both offerings
steps.stepSummary: The animal is slaughtered in the north, its blood goes on the thumbs and toes, it gets סמיכה, נסכים and waving of breast and thigh, and it is eaten only by male כהנים for one day and a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: That אשם must be slaughtered in the north, have its blood put on the thumb and toe, have hands leaned on it, come with wine offerings, have its breast and thigh waved, and be eaten only by male כהנים for one day and the night after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists how this doubtful animal is offered: it gets the strict rules of an אשם and of a שלמים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody knows which offering it really is, every rule of both offerings is kept. The key point is the end: it is eaten only for one day and a night, like an אשם. If it is really a שלמים, it should have had two days, so it loses eating time. That is the difficulty the next steps take up.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering in the northern part of the עזרה, required for an אשם
Putting blood on the מצורע's right thumb and big toe (and ear)
Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before slaughter
Wine poured as an offering together with the animal
Waving the breast and thigh, done with a שלמים
Male כהנים, the only ones allowed to eat an אשם

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the animal stops being an אשם or a שלמים. It is really one of them, we just don't know which, so it is treated strictly both ways.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows רבי שמעון allows a condition on a קרבן, but the shorter eating time is the problem the גמרא has to deal with next.

phrases.english: And that guilt offering requires
slaughter in the north, and placement on the thumbs,
phrases.notes: The blood goes on the right thumb and right big toe of the person, as in ויקרא 14:14.

phrases.english: and placing hands, and libations,
and waving of the breast and thigh,
and it is eaten by males of the priesthood
for a day and a night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the animal from the condition in step 1 is actually offered and eaten.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון allows bringing a קרבן with a condition when one is unsure what he owes
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון lets the doubtful מצורע bring one animal with a two-way condition, even though it is then eaten only one day and a night

steps.title: Mentioning an answer given in מסכת זבחים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that a Sage already answered this point elsewhere, in the perek of 'שחיטת קדשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though the Master answers this in 'שחיטת קדשים'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says that someone already pushed off this proof in another place, and the next line will quote that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line does not give the answer yet. It only points to an answer found in מסכת זבחים. The next step spells out what that answer says.

keyTerms.meaning: Answers, resolves a difficulty
'The Master', a respectful way of referring to a Sage
The name of a section in מסכת זבחים

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא מְפָרֵיק מָר
phrases.english: And even though the Master resolves it
in 'The slaughter of sacrificial animals.'
phrases.notes: This is the name of a section of מסכת זבחים, where this same question came up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא מְפָרֵיק מָר בִּשְׁחִיטַת קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the proof in steps 1-2 by pointing to an answer given elsewhere.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Introduces a rejection of the proof from רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated yet; the next step gives it

steps.title: רבי שמעון allowed it only to help a person
steps.stepSummary: The answer from זבחים: רבי שמעון lets a person bring and stipulate from the start only to fix up a person's status. In general, shortening the eating time is fine after the fact, but not from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that רבי שמעון said one may bring an animal and make a condition from the start only to fix up a person. But in general, after the fact it is fine; from the start it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the answer from זבחים. It limits רבי שמעון's rule to a special case, so it cannot prove a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubtful מצורע has no other way to become טהור, so רבי שמעון lets him make this condition from the start. That does not mean anyone may set up a קרבן in a way that shortens its eating time. Normally that is allowed only בדיעבד, if it already happened, but not לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, before acting
After the fact, once it already happened
To fix up a person, here to let him become טהור
In general, in ordinary cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's doubtful מצורע case is a special allowance to help a person become טהור. In general, shortening a קרבן's eating time is fine only בדיעבד, not לכתחילה.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say shortening the eating time is always forbidden. It says it is fine after the fact, just not something you plan from the start, except to help a person.

phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Shimon said:
one brings and stipulates from the outset —
to fix up a man,
phrases.notes: He means helping the doubtful מצורע become טהור, since he has no other way.

phrases.english: but in general —
after the fact yes, from the outset no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual content of the answer mentioned in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבי שמעון's case as a general proof that one may shorten eating time לכתחילה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is a special allowance meant to help a person become טהור, so no general rule can be learned from it

steps.title: Shortening eating time is a problem for שלמים, not for מנחות
steps.stepSummary: The rule that conditions are only acceptable after the fact applies to שלמים, where the condition cuts down their eating time. With מנחות this problem does not exist, so a condition is fine even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule (only after the fact) applies to שלמים, because the condition cuts down how long they may be eaten, and that brings holy food toward becoming disqualified. But with מנחות, it is allowed even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now replies to the answer from זבחים quoted in step 4. It explains that the 'only after the fact' limit does not apply to מנחות, so the proof from רבי שמעון still works here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים may normally be eaten for two days and a night. Treating them under the stricter rules of an אשם cuts that time down to one day and a night, so meat may go to waste (נותר). A מנחה has no such problem, so the משנה can follow רבי שמעון even if it has the person set a condition from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule only applies to...
He cuts down the time allowed for eating them
Bringing holy food toward becoming disqualified
From the start, as the proper way to act

steps.whatToRemember: Bringing an offering with a condition is only limited where it shortens the eating time (as with שלמים). With מנחות it is fine even from the start.

phrases.english: This applies only to peace offerings,
since he cuts down the time for eating them,
which brings holy food toward becoming disqualified,
but meal offerings – even from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to the answer from זבחים (steps 3-4) by limiting it to שלמים, so the proof holds for מנחות
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Pushes back the זבחים answer, so the proof that the משנה can follow רבי שמעון stands for מנחות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'only after the fact' rule comes from shortening eating time, and that problem does not exist with מנחות

steps.title: רב פפא: Half and half means one tenth made from two tenths
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: under רבי שמעון's half-and-half method, each obligation is made from parts of two separately sanctified עשרונות and two separate לוגין of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: רבי שמעון, who said he should bring half חלות and half רקיקין, has the person bringing one עשרון out of two עשרונות, and one לוג out of two לוגין!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the idea that the משנה can follow רבי שמעון. He points out a problem with how the half-and-half offering is put together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty loaves and wafers come from two עשרונות of flour, each sanctified in its own vessel, with two separate לוגין of oil. If half the חלות and half the רקיקין count as one offering, that one offering is taken from two different sanctified portions, which looks invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick baked loaves (one kind of oven-baked מנחה)
Thin wafers (the other kind of oven-baked מנחה)
A tenth of an איפה, the amount of flour in a regular מנחה
A measure of oil that goes with a מנחה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Rabbi Shimon, who said
"he should bring half loaves and half wafers,"

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא מַיְיתֵי עִשָּׂרוֹן אֶחָד מִשְּׁנֵי עִשָּׂרוֹן,
phrases.english: look, he is bringing one tenth out of two tenths,
and one log out of two logs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the condition problem is solved, a new problem is raised about how the offering is put together
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה can follow רבי שמעון's half-and-half method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each obligation would be made from two separately sanctified עשרונות and לוגין, which looks invalid

steps.title: רבי שמעון holds that one tenth from two tenths is valid
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי שמעון is known to hold that one עשרון from two עשרונות, or one לוג from two לוגין, is valid after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have heard that רבי שמעון said: if he brought one עשרון from two עשרונות, and one לוג from two לוגין, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא by quoting another ruling of רבי שמעון. That ruling shows the problem does not bother him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed a מנחה must come from one sanctified portion. רבי שמעון rules elsewhere that a mixed portion still counts (יצא), so his half-and-half method is consistent with his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard him say (we know his opinion from elsewhere)
He has fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: We have heard that Rabbi Shimon said:
phrases.notes: This is אביי's answer to רב פפא.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הֵבִיא עִשָּׂרוֹן אֶחָד מִשְּׁנֵי עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: If he brought one tenth from two tenths,
and one log from two logs – he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that רבי שמעון's own ruling accepts the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מנחה made from two separate portions would be invalid
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds it is valid, so his method works

steps.title: How is the handful taken from a mixed offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the קמיצה can be done properly when the offering is a mix of חלות and רקיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does he take the handful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the half-and-half offering. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every מנחה needs a קמיצה taken for it. Since nobody knows which kind of offering the person vowed, it is unclear which loaves the handful should be taken from and what it counts for.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a handful from the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
How?

phrases.english: And how does he take the handful?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the mixed offering is valid, asks how its קמיצה works
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the handful is taken and what it counts for in a mixed offering

steps.title: He sets conditions for every possible vow
steps.stepSummary: He sets a condition: if he vowed only חלות or only רקיקין, each handful counts for its own kind; if he vowed half and half, each handful counts for the whole mixed offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sets a condition and says: if I said חלות alone or רקיקין alone, the handful I take from the חלות should count for the חלות, and the handful from the רקיקין for the רקיקין. If I said half רקיקין and half חלות, the handful from the חלות should count for half חלות and half רקיקין, and the handful from the רקיקין should count for half רקיקין and half חלות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The person sets conditions so that the handfuls work whichever vow he actually made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He takes two handfuls, one from the חלות and one from the רקיקין. Each handful's role depends on what he really vowed. That way every possible obligation has a proper קמיצה, and the rest is a gift offering.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets a condition
On their own, only that kind
I take the handful
Half

steps.whatToRemember: With conditions, רבי שמעון's half-and-half method works fully: the offering is valid, and each handful counts for whatever the person really vowed.

phrases.english: He sets a condition and says:

phrases.aramaic: אִי חַלּוֹת לְחוֹדַיְיהוּ, וּרְקִיקִין לְחוֹדַיְיהוּ אֲמַרִי –
phrases.english: If I said loaves alone, or wafers alone –
the handful I take from the loaves should be for the loaves,
the handful I take from the wafers should be for the wafers.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין וּמֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת אֲמַרִי –
phrases.english: If I said half wafers and half loaves –
the handful I take from the loaves
should be for half loaves and half wafers,
and the handful I take from the wafers
should be for half wafers and half loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the קמיצה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He sets conditions so that each handful counts for whatever he really vowed

steps.title: A mixed offering needs one handful taken from the loaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the condition from Step 9. A half-and-half מנחה needs one single קומץ that includes the חלות. A handful taken from only one kind does not seem to do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it requires taking one handful from the loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the condition just suggested for the half-and-half case. This line opens the challenge, and it carries on in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the condition, each handful was taken from just one kind, either חלות or רקיקין. But if the vow was half and half, the offering is one mixed מנחה. A mixed מנחה needs one קומץ that is taken from the חלות as part of it. So a handful from one kind alone seems unable to count for the whole mixed offering.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely: opens a challenge
It requires / it needs
To take the handful (do the קמיצה)
The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Thick loaves, one kind of baked מנחה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the offering is made only of חלות. It is pointing out that the one handful for a mixed offering must include the חלות, and the sentence goes on to finish the requirement.

phrases.english: But it requires taking
phrases.notes: "It" means the half-and-half offering from the condition in Step 9.

phrases.english: one handful from the loaves

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּעֵי מִיקְמָץ חַד קוֹמֶץ מֵחַלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the half-and-half part of the condition proposed in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 9 that, for a half-and-half vow, each handful counts for the whole mixed offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mixed מנחה needs one single handful that includes the חלות. Under the condition, though, each handful was taken from one kind alone, so it cannot properly count for the whole mixed offering.
